Project: Self-Hosted Note Timeline
Component: Token-Based Authentication
Domain: security
Purpose: A dedicated auth module issues and validates access tokens; the project's own README did not mention this, but the real server/auth/ module confirms it exists.
Target file: backend/src/middleware/token-based-authentication.ts
Required export shape: Export the Express middleware function as a named export literally called `middleware`, fully typed - e.g. `import type { Request, Response, NextFunction } from "express"; export function middleware(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void { ... }`. No default export. IMPORTANT: this middleware is mounted globally with app.use(middleware), so it runs on EVERY request to the server - every route, every method, including plain GET requests that carry no body. Unless the purpose says it protects every request (e.g. authentication), first check req.method and req.path and call next() immediately for any request the purpose does not cover; only validate or reject the requests it is actually about. If it checks tokens (e.g. a JWT), it MUST verify the signature before trusting anything in the token: HMAC-SHA256 with createHmac and timingSafeEqual from "node:crypto", keyed by process.env.JWT_SECRET, and reject every token when JWT_SECRET is unset. Decoding a token without verifying its signature is not authentication - anyone could forge one.
Available npm packages: express
Allowed local imports: none - this file must have no local (relative) imports
Architectural constraints already declared for this project: none.

Component: routes table
Domain: database
Purpose: Stores driver id, date, and locations visited.
Target file: backend/src/db/routes-table.ts
Required export shape: import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite" - this is Node's own built-in SQLite module, NOT the "better-sqlite3" npm package, so never import from "better-sqlite3". Export the DatabaseSync instance as a named export `db` (e.g. `export const db = new DatabaseSync(...)`), using `db.exec(sql)` for schema/DDL statements and `db.prepare(sql).run(...)` / `.get(...)` / `.all(...)` for parameterized queries - never string-concatenated SQL. `.all()` and `.get()` return a generic `Record<string, SQLOutputValue>` shape under TypeScript, not your specific row interface, so a direct `as YourType[]` cast will fail to compile - cast through `unknown` first, e.g. `stmt.all() as unknown as Recipe[]`. `DatabaseSync` has no `.query` method, `db.exec` returns void, and these calls are synchronous - do not await them. Do not write the `SQLOutputValue` type yourself. Export an interface for each row shape, and one named function per query the purpose describes, each with fully typed parameters and an explicit return type. No default export.

Allowed local imports: none - this file must have no local (relative) imports

Project: Food Truck Route Planner
Component: Revenue Guard
Domain: security
Purpose: Denies access to the revenue dashboard except to the owner.
Target file: backend/src/middleware/revenue-guard.ts
Required export shape: Export the Express middleware function as a named export literally called `middleware`, fully typed - e.g. `import type { Request, Response, NextFunction } from "express"; export function middleware(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void { ... }`. No default export. IMPORTANT: this middleware is mounted globally with app.use(middleware), so it runs on EVERY request to the server - every route, every method, including plain GET requests that carry no body. Unless the purpose says it protects every request (e.g. authentication), first check req.method and req.path and call next() immediately for any request the purpose does not cover; only validate or reject the requests it is actually about. If it checks tokens (e.g. a JWT), it MUST verify the signature before trusting anything in the token: HMAC-SHA256 with createHmac and timingSafeEqual from "node:crypto", keyed by process.env.JWT_SECRET, and reject every token when JWT_SECRET is unset. Decoding a token without verifying its signature is not authentication - anyone could forge one.

IMPORTANT: this middleware is mounted globally with app.use(middleware), so it runs on EVERY request to the server - every route, every method, including plain GET requests that carry no body. Unless the purpose says it protects every request (e.g. authentication), first check req.method and req.path and call next() immediately for any request the purpose does not cover; only validate or reject the requests it is actually about.
